title: Early Marriage as Countercultural Vision
author: Michael Foster
summary: Foster coins the term 'Two-Percenter' to describe young adults married with at least one child before age 25—statistically 2-4% of that age group today. He argues for this ambitious but achievable target as a cultural corrective to delayed adulthood. The piece shows that historically this was common; now it requires intentional formation and character development. Foster emphasizes the milestones develop discipline rather than being strict rules. Key insight: shifting cultural expectations requires deliberate work to make early marriage, homeownership, and parenthood culturally normal again.
points: Two-Percenter target: married, homeowner, child before 25 (now only 2-4% of age group)
Historically normal; now countercultural marker of discipline, character, intentionality
Does not require following rigid timeline but models the character required
Early milestones develop self-discipline by cutting through cultural foolishness
Culture shift toward two-percenters requires intentional community building and modeling
quotes: I'm trying, in my little corner of the world, to make it less rare again.
Some people might turn the idea of becoming a Two-Percenter into a hard rule. That's not my aim. It's a solid, challenging target that takes focus and discipline.
If you stack those milestones together in the U.S. today: under 25, married, homeowner, and with a child, you're talking about a very small slice of the population.
The character required to get there still gets built. You still have to pass on a lot of the foolishness many twenty-somethings waste time on.
Forty-plus years ago that described a big share of 24-year-olds. Now it's a small minority.” Archived from This is Foster on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
